page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, 16.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and a bundled 150 GB local SSD. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core compute capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing with a score of 3812.16 and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip compression at 40.86 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 16.93 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and memory operations fall mostly into the average tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14889.36 and a PassMark CPU score of 12150.69.

A notable tradeoff is the memory subsystem performance. The PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25% at 1711.85, which aligns with the shared CPU allocation model. Despite this, the server maintains average memory bandwidth speeds, reaching 113.71 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Qualitatively, the server offers balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads, delivering high single-threaded performance relative to its shared-resource profile.

This configuration is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and lightweight database operations. Its average performance in Redis SET operations at 8.73 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 15.01 GB/sec makes it a viable option for web hosting, development environments, and moderate transactional workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or intensive multi-threaded memory access.
